name: robotic_arm
source: Fusion 360 'Full arm (no PCB) v25', 2026-11-07. Zero pose is the CAD pose: arm straight up.
conventions: Every joint and tcp position below is WORLD coordinates in the zero pose (the CAD pose).
All link frames are world-aligned in the zero pose, so a link's frame is just its parent joint's position.
Joint angles here are MODEL angles. firmware_map converts: model = sign * firmware + offset.

joints.name: J4
joints.note: wrist pitch, MG996R. Axis from the J4 drum/horn centre; UNVERIFIED (servo spline may sit 10 mm off)

joints.name: J5
joints.note: wrist roll, MG995. Axis = servo spline, 10 mm off the servo body centre

tcp.note: GUESS. The hand is not in the CAD; this is roughly the palm, ~90 mm past the tool mount. Measure it and update.

firmware_map._note: model_deg = sign * firmware_deg + offset. All signs are UNVERIFIED: jog one joint +10 deg with the twin open and flip its sign here if the twin turns the other way (docs/calibration.md). offset is for a firmware zero that is not the straight-up pose. J3 = +1 is the reading under which the saved poses are physically possible (J2 -120 / J3 +120 folds the arm beside the base instead of through the desk).

gripper.kind: continuous servo on a tendon spool
